name: Mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids
aliases: E471, mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids, glyceryl monostearate, glyceryl monopalmitate, glyceryl monooleate, monostearin, monopalmitin, monoolein, GMS, mono- y diglicéridos de ácidos grasos
what_is: A widely used emulsifier made from glycerol and fatty acids. It helps fat and water stay mixed and is found in products such as sliced bread, margarine, ice cream and baked goods.
why_botia: Mono- and diglycerides are among the most common emulsifiers in supermarket foods: they are found in sliced bread, margarine, ice cream and baked goods. The body digests them like other dietary fats. What BOTIA flags is not their safety — JECFA assigned no numerical intake limit — but their source: the fatty acids may come from plant or animal feedstocks, and the ingredient label normally does not establish which.
can_1: Detect E471 and its common mono- and diglyceride names on an ingredient list.
can_2: Explain that the fatty-acid source may be plant or animal and activate the Animal, Muslim, Texture and E-number layers when source traceability matters.
cannot_1: Determine from the name E471 whether the fatty acids came from plant or animal material when the manufacturer does not disclose the source.
cannot_2: Determine the amount of E471 or the exact mono-/diglyceride composition from the ingredient list.
